To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the influence of gender diversity in the board of directors on corporate social performance (i.e., the degree to which a company meets its social obligations) in publicly held family firms depends on the relative power and legitimacy of women in the board.
the influence of gender diversity on corporate social performance in the context of family firms is contingent on the power of women directors and the type of women directors in the board.
women directors have an impact on family firm’s corporate social performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of women on family firms' CSP, a topic that is largely unexamined in the literature.
the impact of women directors on the corporate social performance of public family firms.
the influence of women on family firms' corporate social responsibility (CSR).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

women directors in the boardroom have a positive influence in the corporate social performance of family firms, especially in the cases where women are not related to the family and have an outsider perspective.
women directors, particularly outsider women, can make a difference to family firm's corporate social performance, but only if their relative influence and legitimacy are high enough.
women directors have a positive influence in family firms' CPS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
family firms with a greater proportion of women on the board are more likely to be associated with higher levels of corporate social performance.
women on boards of family firms have a positive impact on the firm’s CSP.
women directors are not a panacea for improving corporate governance and corporate social performance, but they are important in family firms, especially when the family has lost power in the firm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the influence of gender diversity on family firm boards is contingent on the relative power and legitimacy of women in the boardroom.
family firm boardrooms can be a fertile ground to study gender diversity in corporate boards and its influence on firms' social performance.
family firms are more likely to adopt socially responsible practices when women directors are more powerful and legitimate in the family firm's board.
